The fixed circuit ran on garnet:mock with 100 shots and completed. Counts (QB1 is the left bit, QB2 is the right bit): 00 = 41, 11 = 59. Job ID: 01a15f16-fddb-7145-b9b2-6e73d324b2d2.

The original circuit had two bugs.
1. It used "cx". Garnet does not have that gate. Its native operations are prx, cz, and measure. I replaced the CNOT with the standard native form: prx(angle -pi/2, phase pi/2) on the target, then cz, then prx(angle pi/2, phase pi/2) on the target.
2. It used QB25. Garnet has only QB1 to QB20, so QB25 does not exist. The live garnet:mock architecture lists only two cz pairs that include QB1: QB1-QB2 and QB1-QB4. I picked QB2.

I kept the first gate, prx(pi/2, pi/2) on QB1, which acts as Ry(pi/2). The fixed circuit is: prx(pi/2, pi/2) on QB1, then prx(-pi/2, pi/2) on QB2, then cz on (QB2, QB1), then prx(pi/2, pi/2) on QB2, then measure QB1 and QB2 with key "m". It passed client validation before I submitted it.

On a mock, the gates have no real effect and the results are random, so these counts do not prove entanglement. On a real QPU this circuit would give mostly 00 and 11. My first script crashed after submitting because it called a method that does not exist in iqm-client 35.0.3 (wait_for_results). I fetched the same job by ID and did not resubmit it, so only one job was sent.
